<a id="bodies-and-prose"></a>

# Bodies and Prose

A body is Markdown text in one block. The store keeps it byte for byte after normalization; the manifest only points at it.

`body set` replaces a body, `body append` and `body prepend` extend it, and block `0` creates a new block under the parent. `body get` reads it, optionally a line range, and `body list` lists the blocks of the book.

Text is decoded at the command boundary. A leading UTF-8 byte-order mark is ignored, UTF-16 or UTF-32 with a byte-order mark is transcoded, and Windows line endings become LF in a body. A file without a byte-order mark that is not valid UTF-8, or that contains NUL bytes, is refused with `text.invalid-encoding` and the byte offset. The same rule applies to every `--file` and stdin input, including prose, regions, layout notes, AsciiUI specs, grammar checks and imports.

```text
pecia body set --book guide 0 --parent <chapter> --file chapter.md
pecia body append --book guide <block> --body "One more paragraph."
pecia body get --book guide <block> --lines 1-20
```

`body replace` performs a counted batch replacement. It takes `--find` and `--replace`, or a `--pairs` file, plus `--expect N`. It applies everything in one atomic write and refuses when the count differs.

The prose rule: a body must not contain `#`, `##` or `###` headings. Structure owns headings; `####` and deeper are text. A leading metadata block is not allowed in a body.

Text is normalized on write: line endings become newlines, trailing spaces are trimmed, and the file ends with one newline. A byte-order mark is rejected.

Every prose write runs the grammar gate before the snapshot. That includes `body set`, the append and prepend variants, `body replace`, index prose, the footer, note blocks and layout notes.

`find` searches bodies and titles; `--field body,title` narrows the search and `--context N` prints surrounding lines. Search is read-only and works on closed books. `flush` removes stale transient inputs from `.temp`.

Atomicity is a core guarantee: a mutation locks the book and the block, writes a rollback package, writes the manifest and the bodies, and only then releases the lock. A failed write leaves the previous state intact.

A practical loop is open the book, write or replace a body, run `sync --check`, and close when done. The check and the grammar report tell you what still needs attention before the next render.
